summary: Helga Uebach was a Tibetologist who earned her Ph.D. from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1960–1967). In 1964, she worked as a wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Hellmut Wilhelm was a Sinologist who studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1928–1932). He later served at the University of Washington (~1948–1976) as Professor of Chinese Studies and Associate Director of the Far Eastern Institute.
Helmer Smith worked in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Lund University (~1921–1936) and Uppsala University (~1936–1947).

Helmut Eimer was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Frank-Richard Hamm (~1968–1973). He was attested as holding a post at the University of Bonn from 1991 to 2010.

Helmut Hoffmann specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Freiburg and Berlin under Lüders, Tucci, and Lessing, later holding posts at Munich (1948) and Indiana University (1969–1980).

Helmut Krasser was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held posts at the University of Vienna and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 1991), and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1991–2014).
Helmut Rix, a linguist and Indologist, studied at the University of Würzburg (~1947–1950). He held posts at the University of Regensburg (~1968–1974) and the University of Freiburg (~1974–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Steinkellner (attested 1977–1981). He served as a professor at the University of Vienna (attested 2010–2015) and was a Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

Helmuth von Glasenapp studied Indology and religious studies under Hermann Jacobi and Wanczura, completing Habilitations at Bonn and Berlin. He taught at Bonn and Berlin (1918–1929) before holding chairs at Königsberg (1928–1944) and Tübingen (1946–1959).

Hendrik Kern worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. After studying at Utrecht, Leiden, and under Albrecht Weber (1855–1856), he served as a professor at Leiden University from 1865 to 1903.

Heng Sure is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union (PhD ~1998–2003). His teachers included Hsuan Hua, Edmond Yee, and doctoral supervisor Ronald Y. Nakasone.
Henk Blezer is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his studies at Leiden University (~1987–1997) and later held a post there around 1998.

Henk Bodewitz studied Indology and linguistics at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (PhD ~1961–1973). He served as dean of the Faculty of Arts at Utrecht (1980–1986) and as a professor at Leiden University (1992–2002).
Henri Gaidoz was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at the Lycée Louis-le-Grand (~1855–1860) and under Albrecht Weber in 1865.

Henri Maspero studied Sinology and linguistics at École nationale des langues orientales vivantes. He held posts at École française d'Extrême-Orient (1911), Collège de France as professor (1920–1945), and Maison Franco-Japonaise as director (1928–1930).

Historian Henri Pirenne studied at the University of Liège, Frederick William University Berlin, Leipzig, and Paris. He held academic posts at the University of Liège (~1885–1886) and Ghent University (1886–1930).

Henrik Samuel Nyberg specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University in 1908 and held a post there from approximately 1919 to 1956.

Henry Chung-hung Shiu specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Toronto (completed by 2006) and studied under Shek-wing Tam, Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David Waterhouse, Julia Ching, and Willard Gurdon Oxtoby.

Henry Clarke Warren was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Harvard Oriental Series. He studied at Harvard University (B.A. ~1875–1879), Johns Hopkins University (1879), and under Charles Rockwell Lanman (1879).

Henry George Keene worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the East India Company (~1798–1811) and later at the East India Company College as a professor (~1824–1834).
